scope: Sensor, clock and mounting facts re-measured on OUR production recipe, from all six development recordings

tool.origin: taken from origin/experiments/dolgov (Nikita Dolgov), reviewed by us before adoption
tool.why_adopted: it measures the cross-recording questions our own inspect_bag cannot: capture configuration, clock behaviour over a whole recording, return multiplicity and mounting in the frame the detector works in

two_capture_configurations.reading: doubleT_obstacle is a 360 deg capture on /sensing/lidar/hesai128/pointcloud under frame_id lidar_livox, whose point-time span equals the full 0.100 s frame period; the other five are 120 deg sector captures on /lidar_points under frame_id hesai_lidar whose span is one third of the period. One sensor_rotation and a zero sensor_translation are applied to both.

confirmed_on_our_recipe.independent_reproduction_of_the_mounting: our run reproduces the earlier cross-branch measurement to the precision it reported: sensor height above the bed 1.726 m on doubleT_obstacle against 1.307-1.326 m on the other five, and bed roll -2.945 deg against -0.132..+0.625 deg. doubleT_obstacle is 0.41 m higher and about 3.3 deg different in roll.
confirmed_on_our_recipe.dual_return_multiplexing: exactly 2 slots per emission on every recording with no exception: 460800 emissions over 921600 slots on doubleT_obstacle, 153600 emissions over 307200 slots on each of the other five
confirmed_on_our_recipe.frame_gaps: largest header gap 1.099941 s on roundT_squareT_pressureGate_squareT, 0.700093 s on squareT_platform_squareT_switch and 0.399947 s on doubleT_obstacle, against our track_max_gap_s 0.35 s and frame_max_gap_s 0.5 s
confirmed_on_our_recipe.point_timestamps: header equals the start of the acquisition (header minus first point p50 0.000 s, header minus last point p50 -0.0999/-0.0333 s) and the bag record time sits in a different epoch, about 8.4e8 s away

second_measurement_dual_return_consequen.method: build/adopt-20260920/dual_return_impact.py, which pairs the two slots of every (ring, point-timestamp) emission and measures their separation in the frame the detector reduces in
second_measurement_dual_return_consequen.conclusion: The second slot is almost always the same measurement written twice: identical xyz AND identical intensity in 99.9 per cent of the zero-separation pairs. It is NOT an extra independent ray. Our decision path is largely insulated because the 0.05 m removal voxel merges 98 per cent of the pairs already; the residual 1-2 per cent are genuinely distinct returns from one emission and are legitimately kept.

what_this_changes_in_our_conclusions: Any published number of the form "the recording contains N returns" is about twice the number of independent measurements. The shape of our earlier range and walkway-band statements survives, the magnitudes do not; raw_points, input_valid_points and range_observability returns_before_geometry_voxel all count duplicated slots.

The labelled obstacle recording is the outlier capture configuration of the six. Labels, localization metrics and the continuity-guard status change all lean on it, while the other five are a different sector, a different frame label, a different point-time span and a different mounting. This did not invalidate those results but it does bound them.

Tracking breaks on the recorded gaps: 1.10 s and 0.70 s exceed track_max_gap_s 0.35 s, and the 1.10 s gap also exceeds frame_max_gap_s 0.5 s, which resets odometry and clears the tracker. Per-frame event counts on those stretches are understated.

Deskew must stay off, now for a second measured reason as well as the provenance one: on the five sector recordings the acquisition span is one third of the frame period, and KISS-ICP stretches the supplied normalised range over a full inter-frame increment, so enabling it would over-correct by about three times.

A dual-return sensor is not a reason to add a return-index field: our decoder reads only x, y, z and a timestamp, which is sufficient because the duplicate slot carries no new information and the reduction removes it.
limits: The duplication share is measured on 5-8 scans per recording, not all of them; the pairing rule is exact but the sampling is not exhaustive.
This is a measurement of these six recordings and does not establish sensor model, calibration provenance or hardware detection range.
Nothing in this record changed the detector. It changes what our documents may claim.
